summary: THREE target rows; ONE stored type CONFIRMED (20) and TWO retyped (21, 22 filler -> mixed) with anchors, and the decisive structural finding is that AFL and AFG are NOT two independent witnesses here: AFG's Season-2 table is yakusokunoneverland.fandom's `adaptation_of` field COPIED VERBATIM (ep 20 '145, 146, 147, 148, 149, 150, 151, 152, 153' = the fandom's 145-153; ep 21 '153, 154, 159' = the fandom's identical three-value oddity; ep 22 '165, 166, 167, 168, 169, 170' = the fandom's 165-170), and AFG's own page LINKS to that wiki (its continua cell cites yakusokunoneverland.fandom.com/wiki/Peter_Ratri). PREMISE CHECK FIRST (the TBATE lesson): the task said 'AFG canon ch 145-148 / 153-159 / 165-168'; the LIVE page prints 145-153 / 153,154,159 / 165-170 and carries NO type class at all on any Season-2 row (no red, no blue) -- so AFG makes no filler/canon claim on these rows, only a chapter mapping. AND AFG'S OWN NOTE CONTRADICTS ITS OWN TABLE: 'This second season is an abbreviated version of the events that take place between chapters 38 and 181 ... the main ones being the omission of the Goldy Pond Battle Arc (chapters 75-95) AND THE BATTLE AGAINST THE DEMON QUEEN AND HER NOBLES' -- i.e. AFG itself says the substance of ch 146-159 is omitted while its column prints those numbers. The wave-1 lesson reproduced exactly: AFG's chapter column is a reading-position plateau, its NOTE is the instrument. The same self-contradiction sits inside the fandom: its 'Anime and Manga Differences' page says 'Imperial Capital Battle Arc: The anime LARGELY SKIPS OVER this arc' and 'Return to Grace Field Arc: the anime depicts an ABRIDGED VERSION of this arc' while its episode infoboxes print whole chapter runs -- so the infobox field is a where-are-we-in-the-manga marker, not an adaptation claim. TWO SOURCES BEYOND THE TWO LABELS, used for content: (1) the LICENSOR, neverland-anime.com/story/?id=ep8|ep9|ep10 (live, per-episode official synopses, ja) and (2) en-Wikipedia's 'The Promised Neverland season 2' per-episode ShortSummary block, matched beat-by-beat against the fandom's per-CHAPTER summaries for ch 131-171. ja-Wikipedia's episode list carries no chapter column and no filler marker; it is used only for ROW IDENTITY, which is clean (S2 ep 8 = 2021-03-05, ep 9 = 03-12, ep 10 = 03-19; the 2/12 special 'Guidepost'/17.5 is not one of our rows, so our 23 rows = the fandom's Episode 1-23 with no offset). EP 20 -- FILLER CONFIRMED, AFL is right. No chapter of 145-153 is adapted in substance. The manga's 145-152 is the ROYAL CAPITAL: Oliver and the Goldy Pond survivors bringing horses (145), Geelan's 700-year revenge assault and his backstory and death (146-150), Norman's team wearing Queen Legravalima down and poisoning her (151-152), Emma bursting in too late over a room of corpses (152). NONE of that is in the episode: the Royal Capital is on the fandom's own list of 'Manga locations that did not appear in the anime', Geelan / Legravalima / the Five Regent Houses / Oliver / Gillian / Ayshe / Hayato / Zack never appear in the ep-20 cast list, and the episode's massacre happens in an anime-original Demon Village against two ANIME-ORIGINAL characters (the wiki states flatly: 'Vylk is an anime original character, and as such, he does not appear in the manga'; same sentence for Emma (Demon)). What the episode DOES hold from the source is three slivers: a newly dramatised Lambda flashback of backstory the manga only narrates (119, 124; the facility's destruction is a panel referenced at 129) and which the anime ALREADY delivered as exposition in ep 18; the search for Sonju and Mujika, restaged from 143-144 with Emma and Ray in place of Hayato, Ayshe and Jin and with the assassination attempt removed; and one ch-154 beat (the licensor's EP8 line 'the claim that Norman was not experimented on at Lambda was a lie'). Under the T28 sole-adaptation exception the row does NOT flip: the ch-154 beat is not sole (ep 21 carries it too) and the 143-144 / 151-152 ties are restagings with no page tie. Under the RECAP BOUNDARY the Lambda sequence is newly animated, not recycled -- so it is not weightless, it weighs TOWARD filler, because it adds scenes the source lacks (Peter Ratri personally receiving Norman, Isabella's farewell, Smee dying and handing over the pen). EP 21 -- filler -> MIXED. The episode's own job, per the licensor ('Emma tries to persuade Norman to stop the extermination even now ... she calls out to Norman as if seeing through to his true feelings') and per en-WP ('Emma tells Norman that he should not shoulder the responsibility of saving humanity alone ... Norman relents in his quest to kill all demons and his Lambda followers reluctantly agree'), is chapter 153 'Coward' -- the scene in which Emma and Ray tell Norman he is not alone and Norman breaks down -- plus the opening of 154 (the team accepting the change of plan). That is the Imperial Capital arc's emotional RESOLUTION, adapted nowhere else, and it carries the episode. The rest is anime-original and story-carrying in its own right: Vylk's 700-year backstory and his pen cap containing the Grace Field blueprint AND the Lambda antidote (the wiki: 'In the anime, the Pen Cap is given to Emma by Vylk ... which is not the case in the manga'; the manga's cure is Adam's blood, ch 154), the radio bait about Phil's shipment (the wiki: 'In the anime, the escapees are lured back to Grace Field because Phil and the others getting shipped, which was not the case in the manga'), and Vincent's staged call to Isabella ('nor was Vincent "betraying" Norman by contacting Peter Ratri'). Source + non-source, both story-carrying, in one episode = mixed (T28). EP 22 -- filler -> MIXED. The spine IS ch 166-170 in compressed form and the fandom's own arc page says so ('the anime depicts an abridged version of this arc'): the infiltration of Grace Field to free Phil and the captured children with a blackout and a CCTV takeover (166-167), Peter springing his counter-trap and the children cornered at gunpoint (168-169), and the arc's defining reveal -- Isabella turning her gun on Peter Ratri with every Mama following her (169-170). The original share is equally load-bearing: the hot-air-balloon assault used as a decoy and Vincent's staged betrayal replace the manga's three ground teams and hidden plan, and a demon-civilian uprising led by Mujika, Sonju and the anime-original Vylk replaces the destroyed outer bridge (167) as the answer to Peter's 2000 soldiers -- the wiki calls that last one anime-original in as many words. Mixed, on the same shape Sean already ruled for ep 23 (T6 2026-08-25: 'adapts chs 172-178 beat-for-beat with ruled substitutions -> mixed'); ep 22 is the same shape with more substitution. Chapter 165 (Isabella's confinement, her promotion to Grandmother and her deal with Ratri) is NOT adapted -- the fandom's own ep-21 'Research elements' say 'Isabella became a grandma for unknown reasons' and 'It is unknown what happened to the previous grandmother', which is precisely 165's content. WHICH SOURCE LIED: animefillerguide's chapter column, by reprinting a fandom infobox field that is a manga-timeline marker as though it were coverage -- and it lied about ep 20 in a way its own NOTE refutes. AFL was right about 20 and wrong about 21 and 22, in the ordinary way (it typed a whole compressed block by its worst episode).

anchors.note: A4 END = 154, the furthest mainline chapter adapted in running order; A10 START = 153, the chapter the episode opens on. Ch 153 'Coward' is the episode's spine and its weight is SIGNIFICANT -- because it is the Imperial Capital arc's resolution and it is what the episode is FOR: Emma and Ray telling Norman he is not alone, and Norman breaking down. Three independent readings agree on the beat: the licensor's EP9 synopsis (neverland-anime.com: 'Emma persuades Norman to stop the extermination even now, but Norman will not listen to her words. Emma calls out to him as if seeing through to his true feelings'), en-WP ('Emma tells Norman that he should not shoulder the responsibility of saving humanity alone, but he reveals that because of the drugs administered at Lambda 7214 he does not have long to live'), and the fandom's episode plot ('He breaks down crying in front of Emma, crushed by the suffering he has experienced'). The manga's ch 153 is the same scene ('Emma and Ray in unison tell Norman he is not alone anymore ... Norman finally breaks down, cries and runs to his friends begging them for help'). It is relocated -- the manga stages it in the throne room over Legravalima's corpses, the anime in the poisoned village -- which under the T28 faithfulness clause is a `divergence` on a source scene, not a disqualification. Material is NEW: no other episode adapts ch 153. Ch 154's OPENING is adapted too and its weight is SLIVER -- because it is one scene, not the chapter: Norman's Lambda followers accepting the change of plan (en-WP: 'his Lambda followers reluctantly agree'; the fandom: Vincent angry, Cislo talking him down, Barbara answering that Norman matters more than revenge). Its other beats are split or replaced -- the 'Norman lied about not being experimented on' reveal is in ep 20 per the licensor's EP8 synopsis, and 154's Adam-blood cure is replaced by Vylk's anime-original pen antidote -- so NO episode adapts ch 154 in full. The END still advances to 154 under the A47 convention (advance unless the tail is <=5 pages or teaser-worded; neither applies, and 'unquantified' is not evidence of small -- the Dai wave-13 ruling). Volume 18 = ch 153-161, which agrees with the stored boundary table. NOT anchored on 159: AFG and the fandom both print '153, 154, 159' for this row, but ch 159 is the aftermath of a queen battle the anime never staged (the wiki: the anime 'largely skips over' the Imperial Capital Battle Arc; the Royal Capital is on its list of locations that never appear) -- the episode's only tie to 159 is the structural pivot 'the remaining threat is Peter Ratri', which is a loose parallel, not coverage.

A4 END = 170; A10 START = 166. Weight: SIGNIFICANT -- because the five chapters ARE the episode's plot from end to end, compressed roughly one chapter per act: 166 (the infiltration of Grace Field and the blackout to free the hostages -- 'Someone has managed to enter Grace Field House electrical room, causing a blackout' vs the anime's 'Once the lights were shut down, Jemima leads the children to the elevator'), 167 (the takeover of the House's system and the guards lured into one place), 168-169 (Peter springing the counter-trap, the children at gunpoint, Peter summoning the Mamas) and 169-170 (Isabella turning her gun on Peter and every Mama following her -- the arc's defining reveal, and 170 is the chapter that explains why they do it). The licensor's EP10 synopsis carries the same spine (neverland-anime.com: the balloon leak, the shipment at the House, Jemima taking Emma's message, the children reaching the elevator, 'their way blocked by Peter and a large number of armed Sisters led by Isabella, now Grandma'), and en-WP's summary and the fandom's plot agree with it. START is 166 and NOT 165: ch 165 is Isabella's confinement, her promotion to Grandmother and her deal with Ratri, and the anime never adapts it -- the fandom's own 'Research elements' for ep 21 read 'Isabella became a grandma for unknown reasons' and 'It is unknown what happened to the previous grandmother'. END is HELD at 170 and does NOT advance to 171 under R3-before-A47 (the Dai wave-14 existence clause): only ONE source credits a 171 beat (en-WP's 'after she reveals that the deadly chips in their chests having been hacked and nullified' = ch 171's heart-chip beat); the fandom's episode plot and AFG both stop at 170, and 171's own substance (Leuvis revealing the evil blood's truth at the Royal Capital) is never animated. Volume 19 = 162-171, which agrees with the stored boundary table.

continue_points.note: [None] Ends INSIDE ch 154 (only 154's opening scene is adapted; the Adam-blood thread is replaced), so the continue is in the straddled chapter -- C1. This is deliberately NOT a C2 parity value: parity is for material the anime covers LATER, and the anime never covers any of it. NAME THE GAPS ON ARRIVAL: ch 146-152 (Geelan's assault and death, the battle against Queen Legravalima and the Five Regent Houses) are never adapted, and ch 155-165 (the Queen's second form and true death, Mujika's origin, the aftermath, Peter's deal, the High Priest, Mujika and Sonju's arrest, Isabella's promotion) are never adapted either -- ep 22 resumes at 166.

[None] Ep 22 finishes ch 170, so the next unread chapter is 171 -- and 171 is never adapted (its Grace Field half is a single-source fragment inside ep 22; its Royal Capital half, Leuvis revealing that the evil blood is not a poison, is not in the anime at all). The stored ep-23 anchor STARTS at 172, so 171 sits in the gap and the reader should read it: again NOT a parity value, because nothing later covers it.

anchor_hostile.why: A1 -- the row is FILLER (stored type confirmed) and filler rows never carry anchors. Stated positively so the AFG/fandom '145-153' is not re-imported later: the episode adapts none of 145-152 in substance. Its three source ties are all slivers and are delivered as annotations instead -- loose_parallel{143-144} (the search for Sonju and Mujika), loose_parallel{151-152} (the extermination executing and Emma arriving too late, restaged in an anime-original village against anime-original characters), and graft{154} (the licensor's EP8 reveal that Norman lied about the Lambda experiments). The A1 call is not a 'looks anchorable but is typed filler' case: there is no numbered chapter whose pages this episode animates.

annotations.note: weight: SLIVER -- because it is a restaging, not an adaptation: the manga's search party for Sonju and Mujika is Don, Gilda, Hayato, Ayshe and her dogs (135, 143) and it ends with Sonju turning Norman's assassination attempt back on Jin and the Lambda irregulars (144); the anime's is Emma, Ray, Don and Gilda tracking them by bird migration, with no assassination attempt and no Ayshe or Hayato in the episode's cast list at all. No page tie. NOT adapted properly anywhere else either -- ch 143-144's actual content is never animated.

weight: SLIVER -- because only the SHAPE survives. In the manga Norman's team wears Legravalima down and drives the poison into her (151), the poison spreads 'only in specific areas', the Queen is felled, and Emma bursts into a room of corpses too late while Norman imagines a CHILD EMMA tugging his cloak (152). In the anime there is no Queen, no Geelan, no Five Regent Houses and no Royal Capital -- the fandom lists the Royal Capital under 'Manga locations that did not appear in the anime' and its Anime-and-Manga-Differences page says 'the anime largely skips over this arc. While Norman's Massacre of the Demons occurs in the anime, it is very different from how it went in the manga'; AFG's own header note independently lists 'the battle against the demon queen and her nobles' as omitted. The massacre is moved to an anime-original Demon Village and its victims are Vylk and Emma (Demon), both stated by the wiki to be anime-original characters, and the child apparition is INVERTED (Emma sees child Norman). No page tie.

weight: SLIVER -- because it is one reveal inside an otherwise original episode. The licensor's EP8 synopsis (neverland-anime.com/story/?id=ep8) opens 'Norman coughs blood from a seizure. It was a lie that Norman had not been experimented on at Lambda' -- that is ch 154's beat ('Norman even lied to his team that he wasn't experimented on so they wouldn't worry'). It is NOT sole (ep 21 restates it as Norman's level-4 condition), so the T28 sole-adaptation exception is checked and FAILS on its first half; and a single reveal is not a story-carrying share, so it fails the materiality bar too. Ch 154's opening is adapted properly in ep 21 (see that row's anchor); no episode adapts 154 in full.

The episode's first act is a newly animated Lambda 7214 flashback -- Peter Ratri receiving Norman, Isabella's farewell, the cognitive tests, Smee handing over the pen as he dies, the bomb and the escape. This is NOT a recap and the recap clause does not apply (the RECAP BOUNDARY, Sean 2026-09-02): it is new-drawn footage of significant length, not re-shown footage, so it is anime production that shapes the episode. Its factual content is the manga's backstory as NARRATED at ch 119 and ch 124 (Cislo, Barbara and Vincent describing Lambda, and Norman freeing them) with the facility's destruction referenced at ch 129 -- the manga never dramatises the escape -- and the anime had already delivered that account in ep 18 (en-WP ep 18: 'Norman explains ... he escaped with some other children with the help of a supporter of Minerva called Smee and they destroyed the facility'). Because it adds scenes the source lacks, it weighs toward filler, which with an otherwise original remainder is why the row stays filler rather than becoming mixed.

The source scene is RELOCATED and its surroundings replaced: the manga's persuasion happens in the throne room immediately after the Queen's massacre, the anime's in the poisoned Demon Village with Sonju present. Under the T28 faithfulness clause a relocation of the source's own events keeps the material canon; it is recorded here so the anchor is not read as a faithful-adaptation claim.

weight: SLIVER -- because it is one conversation pulled forward, not the chapter. Ch 165's second half is Peter Ratri telling Isabella that Lambda 7214 will rise again and the farms be converted to Lambda-style farms; the anime plays that conversation in ep 21, restaged with a demon superior instead of Isabella (the fandom: 'Ratri explains his plan to expand the Lambda drug-based development to other farms, demolishing the need for high-class farms such as Grace Field'; en-WP: 'Ratri plans to expand the Lambda model of drug-based brain development'). Ch 165's FIRST half -- Isabella's confinement, her acceptance of death, her promotion and her deal with Ratri -- is never adapted; the fandom's own ep-21 Research elements say 'Isabella became a grandma for unknown reasons'. The END therefore does not move to 165, and ep 22 starts at 166.

weight: SLIVER -- because only the OUTCOME is carried. The manga's 155-159 is the Queen's second form, her true death, Sonju's and Mujika's origins and the aftermath, with Mujika and Sonju feeding the demons her blood so they stop degenerating (Imperial Capital Battle Arc page). The anime keeps only the blood-cure and the closing pivot 'the one remaining threat is Peter Ratri' (159), staged in the village with Vylk. AFG and the fandom both list '159' on this row; that is the tie, and it is not coverage -- ch 155-159 are never adapted.

The episode's anime-original share, named so the mixed typing is auditable. All four are stated as anime-original by the fandom's Anime-and-Manga-Differences page: (a) Vylk, an anime-original character, gives Emma the pen cap, and it contains BOTH the Grace Field blueprint and the cure for the Lambda side effects -- 'which is not the case in the manga', where the cure is Adam's blood (154); (b) the escapees are lured back to Grace Field by news that Phil and the others are being shipped -- 'which was not the case in the manga', where Peter simply kidnaps the hideout children (161); (c) Vincent's call to Isabella -- 'nor was Vincent "betraying" Norman by contacting Peter Ratri'; (d) Vylk's 700-year survivor backstory. This share is story-carrying, which is why the row is mixed and not canon.

weight: SIGNIFICANT -- because five chapters are compressed into the episode's whole spine: the infiltration and blackout to free the hostages, the takeover of the House's systems, Peter's counter-trap and the children at gunpoint, and Isabella turning on Peter with the Mamas behind her. The fandom's Return to Grace Field Arc page states the shape in its own words -- 'The anime depicts an abridged version of this arc and the central event, the Return to Grace Field, is very different from how it was in the manga'. Material is NEW throughout: no earlier episode touches 166-170.

The episode's anime-original share, named so the mixed typing is auditable. The manga's operation is three ground teams (Emma's, Oliver's, Vincent's) with a hidden endgame and the outer bridge destroyed to strand Peter's 2000 soldiers (166-167). The anime replaces the means end to end: a hot-air-balloon assault used as a decoy, Vincent's staged betrayal feeding Peter the balloon plan, and -- the fandom's words -- 'Also in the anime, Sonju, Mujika and many other demons civilians start a revolt and break in to Grace Field, which does not happen in the manga', with the anime-original Vylk leading it. Story-carrying original material alongside a story-carrying source share = mixed.

Ch 165 is NOT adapted. Its first half (Isabella in confinement, her acceptance of death, the demons' announcement of her promotion, and Peter's offer of 'real freedom' which she takes) is the explanation of a fact the anime simply shows: the fandom's own ep-21 Research elements read 'Isabella became a grandma for unknown reasons' and 'It is unknown what happened to the previous grandmother'. Its second half is pulled into ep 21 (see the rearranged{165} annotation there). This is why the ep-22 START is 166 and not 165.

weight: SLIVER, and SINGLE-SOURCE. en-WP's ep-22 summary says the Mamas follow Isabella 'after she reveals that the deadly chips in their chests having been hacked and nullified' -- that is ch 171's beat (Peter tries to trigger the Mamas' heart chips 'but the system is still down'). Neither the fandom's episode plot nor the licensor's EP10 synopsis mentions it, and AFG stops at 170. Under R3-before-A47 the END is held at 170; the fragment is recorded here instead. Ch 171 is otherwise never adapted.

type_corrections.why: T28 materiality, both shares story-carrying. SOURCE SHARE, weight SIGNIFICANT: ch 153 in full (Emma and Ray convince Norman he is not alone; Norman breaks down and abandons the extermination) plus the opening of 154 (his Lambda followers accepting it). This is the Imperial Capital Battle arc's resolution, it resolves the season's central conflict, it is what the licensor's own EP9 synopsis is about, and it is adapted in no other episode. NON-SOURCE SHARE, also story-carrying: Vylk's pen cap containing the blueprint and the Lambda antidote (the manga's cure is Adam's blood), the radio bait about Phil's shipment as the lure back to Grace Field (the manga has Peter kidnap the hideout children), Vincent's staged call to Isabella, and Vylk's 700-year backstory -- all four stated to be anime-original by the fandom's Anime-and-Manga-Differences page. Source + non-source in one episode, neither a sliver = mixed, not filler and not canon. AFL typed the whole compressed block filler by its worst rows; on this row it is wrong.

T28 materiality. SOURCE SHARE, weight SIGNIFICANT: ch 166-170 compressed into the episode's entire spine -- the infiltration and blackout, the systems takeover, Peter's counter-trap and the standoff, and Isabella's betrayal of Peter with the Mamas behind her, which is the arc's defining reveal. The fandom's own arc page calls the anime's version 'an abridged version of this arc'. NON-SOURCE SHARE, also story-carrying: the balloon-decoy assault and Vincent's staged betrayal in place of the manga's three ground teams, and the demon-civilian uprising led by Vylk in place of the destroyed outer bridge as the answer to Peter's 2000 soldiers -- the last stated as anime-original by the wiki. Ch 165 is not adapted at all. This is the same shape Sean already ruled MIXED for ep 23 (T6, 2026-08-25: 'adapts chs 172-178 beat-for-beat with ruled substitutions'), one step further along the substitution axis, so mixed is the consistent call -- canon would overclaim the invented mechanism, filler would deny a five-chapter spine.

CONFIRMED AS STORED — CONFIRMATION, not a change -- AFL is right and this is the result. Chapter accounting: ch 145-152's content is the Royal Capital (Oliver's horses, Geelan's revenge assault and death, the battle against Legravalima, Emma arriving too late over a room of corpses) and none of it is in the episode -- the Royal Capital is on the fandom's list of manga locations that never appear in the anime, Geelan and Legravalima and the Five Regent Houses are absent from the cast list, and both the fandom ('the anime largely skips over this arc') and AFG's own header note ('the omission of ... the battle against the demon queen and her nobles') say so in prose. The episode is a newly animated Lambda flashback plus an anime-original massacre in an anime-original Demon Village against two anime-original characters. Its three source ties are slivers (143-144 restaged, 151-152 in shape only, one ch-154 reveal); the sole-adaptation exception is checked and fails -- the 154 beat is not sole and the 143-144/151-152 ties are not page ties. Zero standing in the source's own pages = filler (T27).

structure.notes: ROW IDENTITY FIRST (R20). Our 23 rows = the fandom's Episode 1-23 with no offset: the fandom's List of Episodes prints S2 as 1-11 with the cumulative names Episode 13-23, and the 2021-02-12 special 'Guidepost' is listed as 5.5 / Episode 17.5 and is NOT one of our rows. ja-WP's 各話リスト prints the same run with 特別編「道標」 on 2/12 as an unnumbered row. Dates check: our 20 = 2021-03-05, 21 = 03-12, 22 = 03-19, matching fandom and ja-WP; all Fridays, the season's slot. AFG numbers 13-23 with (01)-(11) sub-numbers, same space. AFG AND THE FANDOM ARE ONE LINEAGE ON THIS SERIES -- do not count them as two. AFG's S2 chapter cells are the fandom `adaptation_of` field verbatim, including the three-value oddity '153, 154, 159' on ep 21, and AFG's own continua cell hyperlinks yakusokunoneverland.fandom.com/wiki/Peter_Ratri. The AFG S2 table carries NO type class on any row (no red, no blue), so the 'AFG canon' side of the T4 flag is an absence-of-class read, not a positive typing claim. PREMISE CHECK: the task's 'AFG canon ch 145-148 / 153-159 / 165-168' is not what the live page prints -- it prints 145-153 / 153,154,159 / 165-170. Argued from the live page throughout. THE TWO CONTENT SOURCES BEYOND AFL/AFG: (1) neverland-anime.com/story/?id=ep6..ep11 -- the licensor's own per-episode synopses, live, in Japanese, one paragraph each; (2) en-Wikipedia 'The Promised Neverland season 2', whose ShortSummary block is written independently of the fandom (it uses 'city' where the fandom says 'village', and it carries the heart-chip line the fandom lacks). Both were matched against the fandom's per-CHAPTER summaries for ch 117-171, which are a different artifact from the episode infoboxes and disagree with them -- that disagreement is the core evidence. SEASON SHAPE, for context: en-WP's lede states the season 'adapted the story arc Promised Forest (chapters 38-52) before turning towards an anime original direction starting within the beginning of the Search For Minerva arc, all the while retaining a few themes and plot points of the original manga'. That is a BLOCK statement and it is not how these rows were typed -- each was typed on its own content, which is why 20 comes out filler and 21-22 come out mixed. AUTHOR PARTICIPATION, considered and REJECTED as an adoption basis: en-WP cites ANN (2020-12-06) that Kaiu Shirai collaborated on Season 2's scripts. That is participation in the ANIME, not incorporation into the source: the manga finished at ch 181 in June 2020, seven months before S2 aired, so nothing from the anime could be written back into it. Per the standing rule (a blanket story credit is not an adoption basis; the author basis requires the source's author writing the anime material's EVENTS into the source line) no adopted{author} annotation is proposed on any row. CHAPTER SPACE: one space, the manga's own 1-181; the stored volume table was used to set the anchors' volumes (v18 = 153-161 for ep 21, v19 = 162-171 for ep 22) and both agree.
structure.unresolved: (1) Rows 16-19 carry stored types (16 mixed, 17 mixed, 18 canon, 19 mixed) but NO anchors, and the zone between the stored ep15 -> 50 and my proposed ep21 -> 154 will now interpolate across them. AFG/fandom map 16 = 73 + 104-109, 17 = 118, 18 = 119-126, 19 = 127-130; en-WP's per-episode summaries for 18 and 19 do read as genuine coverage of ch 119-130 (Norman's Lambda account, the demon-evolution lecture, the degeneration drug, meeting Cislo/Barbara/Vincent, Mujika's 700-year history, the five-day deal), so ep 18 in particular looks anchorable at ~126 -- but that is OUTSIDE this ask and I did not verify it to anchor standard. Either anchor 16-19 in a follow-up or add an A42 zone acknowledgement, or the interpolation between 50 and 154 will show false positions for five rows. (2) Open flag #767 is untouched: AFG's continua text says 'The anime ended at episode 23 ... which corresponds to Chapter 172, 173 and 174' and recommends starting at 175, MU says 181, and the stored ep-23 anchor is 178 [172] from the curated batch-17 verdict. My ep-22 continue of 171 sits below the stored ep-23 START of 172 and is consistent with it; the 174-vs-178 question is a separate ask. (3) The existing A43 divergence on eps 16-22 ('compresses ch 53-181') still fits as a zone note, but its chapters field is prose rather than a comma-separated chapter list; if 21 and 22 gain anchors it may be worth narrowing it to 16-20 so the annotation does not read as a coverage claim over the two anchored rows.

flags_for_sean: COUNT AFL AND AFG AS ONE-AND-A-HALF SOURCES ON THIS SERIES, NOT TWO. AFG's Promised Neverland S2 chapter column is yakusokunoneverland.fandom's `adaptation_of` infobox field copied verbatim (the ep-21 value '153, 154, 159' is the fingerprint) and AFG's page links back to that wiki. Any T4 flag that treats 'AFG maps chapters' as an independent positive claim against AFL will keep firing on this series, and on any series where AFG sourced a fandom.

AFG'S OWN HEADER NOTE REFUTED ITS OWN TABLE ON THIS SERIES, in one sentence: 'This second season is an abbreviated version of the events that take place between chapters 38 and 181 ... the main ones being the omission of the Goldy Pond Battle Arc (chapters 75-95) and the battle against the demon queen and her nobles' -- while the table prints 145-153 on ep 20. If the flag reads AFG's note as well as its column, this contradiction resolves itself before a research slot is spent. Worth considering as a cheap pre-filter.

A FANDOM CAN CONTRADICT ITSELF ACROSS PAGE TYPES, and the prose page wins. Here the episode infoboxes print whole chapter runs while the same wiki's 'Anime and Manga Differences' page says the Imperial Capital Battle Arc is 'largely skipped' and lists the Royal Capital, Paradise Hideout, Goldy Pond and Seven Walls under 'Manga locations that did not appear in the anime'. Same shape as the toriko plateau: an infobox chapter field can be a where-are-we marker.
